entry_state: Capped proportional allocation respects asset floors and preserves any unallocated residual. Reversal uses the depreciated no-impairment ceiling,retains zero goodwill and leaves the zero-weight extension unresolved. Separate provisions need a present obligation and supported measurement. The production example now asks why low output cannot load all idle-capacity costs into remaining stock.
exit_state: Production allocates fixed overhead using supported normal capacity,caps high-output allocation at incurred cost,and expenses unused capacity and excluded costs. Cash reconciliation retains depreciation embedded in inventory. The restoration method separates new estimates from discount unwinding and preserves asset-model-specific profit/OCI treatment. Its full cash history leaves the settlement classification explicitly unresolved;the changed-obligations discussion continues.
findings: The production arms explicitly vary output,sales and variable spending. Their comparison does not imply equal total spending or after-tax statutory statements.
The low-output bridge66+60-116=10 agrees with cash400-390. Adding only48 depreciation while removing all116 stock would be wrong;the alternative must remove cash-cost stock104.

The restoration examples retain the hypothetical cost-model ceiling and separate passage-of-time finance expense. Their cash bridge does not invent a settlement classification. No confirmed new defect.
